activity.notes: Contemporary chronicle tradition, as assessed in historical scholarship, associates the widowed queen Goiswintha and bishop Uldila with opposition to Reccared and a palace conspiracy conventionally placed in 589. This is a REPRESENTATIVE POINT for a reported court event, not a 589 reign, proof of a formal public office, or a secure death date; conflicting death-year conventions (588/589) remain unresolved, and hostile confessional portrayals are treated critically.

sources.title: María Rosario Valverde Castro (2008), Mujeres «viriles» en la Hispania visigoda. Los casos de Gosvinta y Benedicta, Studia Historica. Historia Medieval 26, pp.17–44
sources.citation_text: Researches Gosvinta's political agency and explicitly cautions that although the marriage to Athanagild is attested, the wedding's precise date is unknown.

sources.title: Ana María Jiménez Garnica (2008), Gosuintha, el fracaso de una coniux real, Studia Historica. Historia Antigua 26
sources.citation_text: University of Salamanca focused study of queen Gosuintha's marital and royal political position under Athanagild, Liuvigild, and the subsequent royal court; interpret court claims critically.

sources.title: Barroso Cabrera, Morín de Pablos & Sánchez Ramos (2023), Gallaecia Gothica, Archaeopress
sources.citation_text: Scholarly analysis of late sixth-century Visigothic conflicts explicitly identifies Queen Goiswintha and Arian Bishop Uldila in the 589 court conspiracy against Reccared.
